{{nihongo|'''Morokuchi Shrine'''|諸口神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

It is located facing east at the tip of {{ill|Cape Mihama|Q11489198|qid=Q11489198}}. A red torii visible even from the opposite shore stands along the sea in front.

It is jointly managed by the priest of {{ill|Heda Shrine|Q92443788|qid=Q92443788}} in the same Heda district<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20210920093819/https://ananweb.jp/news/373262/amp/ Hiroyuki Ehara: "I felt immeasurable energy" - two spiritual spots in Numazu] - {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=anan}} 2021/9/18</ref>.

=== Overview ===
Founding is unknown. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} presumed to be one of the two "Kunitama-no-Mikoto Shrines" listed in the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|ja|伊豆国の式内社一覧|qid=Q11380552|lt=Naka District section of Izu Province}} in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'.

From the Jinmyōchō description, the original enshrined deities are inferred as "Moroki-hime, Kunitama-hime, and Tachibana-hime," and the present name "Morokuchi" is thought to derive from that "Moroki"<ref name="yuisho">Precinct origin board</ref>. As a goddess, it was long identified with {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Benten}} and revered by fishermen<ref name="yuisho"/>.

In August {{ill|1879|Q7783|qid=Q7783}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 12), it was designated village shrine. === Festivals ===
* Grand annual festival: April 4

=== Surroundings ===
* To the south-southeast in front are beaches such as "Kobunegahama" and "Mihama Beach."
* On the west side behind the shrine are the {{ill|Heda Shipbuilding Museum|Q11554523|qid=Q11554523|lt=Heda Shipbuilding Local History Museum}} and the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Suruga Bay Deep Sea Aquarium}}.

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Izuhakone Railway|Q864568|qid=Q864568}} "{{ill|Shuzenji Station|Q7505799|qid=Q7505799}}" then {{ill|Tokai Bus|Q11527778|qid=Q11527778}} (bound for Heda)
** Get off at "Heda" bus stop, then walk 20 minutes, circling in from the southeast along the coast.
